capabilities: Render ```cornell``` code blocks as a two-column cue/notes layout
Configure headers, borders, and column widths globally or per block with directives
Embed Markdown content (lists, tables, code blocks, callouts, math, Mermaid, images, wikilinks) in both columns
Stack columns vertically on narrow screens for mobile
Store content as plain text readable without the plugin
disambiguation: It does not help write or structure notes while typing; it only renders an existing ```cornell``` fence in Reading view.
extras: Not yet in the community plugin store (installable manually or via BRAT); README documents known limitations: Live Preview is not supported (Reading view only) and ~sub~/^sup^ syntax is not rendered.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to render the Cornell Notes two-column study layout, which otherwise has to be faked with tables or HTML.
summary: Fenced-block renderer that displays ```cornell``` code blocks as a two-column Cornell Notes layout (cue column plus notes column) in Reading view.
